goal: Produce a half-year (Jan-Jun 2026) sales review of data/orders.json covering headline totals, regional breakdowns, top customers, the monthly trend, refund behaviour by category, product-level insights, and a region x category matrix.
conventions: Order revenue = quantity * unit_price. 'Net revenue' ALWAYS means the sum of revenue over orders with status 'completed' only (refunded and cancelled orders are excluded). 'Gross revenue' means the sum over ALL orders regardless of status. All money values rounded to 2 decimals. All percentages rounded to 2 decimals and expressed as a number out of 100 (e.g. 30.32, not 0.3032).

steps.title: Headline totals and status mix
steps.instructions:
Using data/orders.json (all Jan-Jun 2026), report the headline figures. Revenue of an order = quantity * unit_price. Report EXACTLY these 8 lines and nothing else, in this order and format:
total_orders: <int>
completed_orders: <int>
refunded_orders: <int>
cancelled_orders: <int>
gross_revenue_all_statuses: <2dp>
net_revenue_completed: <2dp>
refunded_revenue: <2dp>
average_order_value_completed: <2dp>
Where gross_revenue_all_statuses sums every order regardless of status; net_revenue_completed sums only status='completed'; refunded_revenue sums only status='refunded'; average_order_value_completed = net_revenue_completed / completed_orders. Do not compute anything by hand - use the provided aggregation tools.
steps.expected_result: total_orders: 400; completed_orders: 300; refunded_orders: 51; cancelled_orders: 49; gross_revenue_all_statuses: 482245; net_revenue_completed: 350507; refunded_revenue: 66733; average_order_value_completed: 1168.36
steps.note: FAIL (round 1). Worker hit the 50-row cap of query_orders, could not reach the full dataset and marked itself blocked. No aggregation tool existed.
steps.result: s1: BLOCKED - Query tool limited to 50 rows max (no pagination/date filtering). Retrieved only January 2026 data. Cannot access complete Jan-Jun 2026 dataset from data/orders.json with current tools. Requires: aggregation API, file access capability, or query tool with date range filtering.

steps.title: Regional breakdown of net revenue
steps.instructions:
Break NET revenue (status='completed' only, revenue = quantity * unit_price) down by region. Rank regions from highest to lowest net revenue. Output EXACTLY one line per region in this format, ranked:
<region>: <net_revenue 2dp> | orders=<int> | aov=<2dp> | share=<2dp>%
where aov = net revenue of that region / number of completed orders in that region, and share = that region's net revenue as a percentage of TOTAL net revenue across all regions. Then a final line:
leader_gap: <2dp>
which is the net revenue of the #1 region minus the net revenue of the #2 region. Use the aggregation tools; do not sum rows by hand.

steps.note: FAIL (round 1). Worker pulled 50 raw rows per region (200/400 rows), did the arithmetic mentally and reported a truncated sample as if complete: APAC 49804 vs 106288. All four regions, aovs, shares and leader_gap wrong.

steps.title: Top customers and revenue concentration
steps.instructions:
Rank customers by NET revenue (status='completed' only, revenue = quantity * unit_price). Output EXACTLY the top 5 customers, one per line, ranked highest first:
<rank>. <customer_id>: <net_revenue 2dp> | orders=<int>
where orders = that customer's number of completed orders. Then exactly these three final lines:
distinct_customers_with_completed_orders: <int>
top5_net_revenue: <2dp>
top5_share_of_net_revenue: <2dp>%
where top5_net_revenue is the sum of the 5 customers' net revenue and top5_share_of_net_revenue is that sum as a percentage of total net revenue across all customers. Use the aggregation tools.

steps.title: Monthly trend January to June 2026
steps.instructions:
Compute the monthly NET revenue trend (status='completed' only, revenue = quantity * unit_price), bucketing by calendar month of the order date. Output EXACTLY one line per month in chronological order (2026-01 through 2026-06):
<YYYY-MM>: <net_revenue 2dp> | orders=<int> | mom=<2dp>%
where mom is the month-over-month percentage change in net revenue versus the previous month; for the first month (2026-01) write mom=n/a. Then exactly these two final lines:
best_month: <YYYY-MM> (<net_revenue 2dp>)
worst_month: <YYYY-MM> (<net_revenue 2dp>)
Use the aggregation tools; do not bucket dates by hand.
steps.note: FAIL (round 1). Only reached early April because raw-row pulls were capped; emitted 4 months instead of 6 and every monthly figure and MoM% wrong.

steps.title: Refund behaviour by category
steps.instructions:
Analyse refunds per product category. Revenue of an order = quantity * unit_price. For EACH of the 4 categories output one line, ranked by refunded_revenue from highest to lowest:
<category>: refunded_revenue=<2dp> | refunded_orders=<int> | total_orders=<int> | refund_rate_by_orders=<2dp>% | refunded_share_of_gross=<2dp>%
where total_orders counts ALL orders of that category regardless of status, refund_rate_by_orders = refunded_orders / total_orders * 100, and refunded_share_of_gross = refunded_revenue / gross revenue of that category (all statuses) * 100. Then exactly these two final lines:
total_refunded_revenue: <2dp>
highest_refund_rate_by_orders: <category> (<2dp>%)
Use the aggregation tools.

steps.title: Region x category matrix and regional refund rates
steps.instructions:
Build a region x category matrix of NET revenue (status='completed' only, revenue = quantity * unit_price). Output EXACTLY 16 lines, iterating regions in alphabetical order (AMER, APAC, EMEA, LATAM) and within each region categories in alphabetical order (accessories, hardware, services, subscription):
<region>/<category>: <net_revenue 2dp>
Then exactly these lines:
top_cell: <region>/<category> (<2dp>)
Then for each region in alphabetical order, one line naming that region's largest category by net revenue:
<region>_top_category: <category> (<2dp>)
Then for each region in alphabetical order, one line with the refund rate by ORDER COUNT over ALL statuses:
<region>_refund_rate: <2dp>%
where refund rate = refunded orders in region / total orders in region * 100. Use the aggregation tools; do not cross-tabulate by hand.
